metadata.source: GPT video descriptions from UCA timestamp annotations

final_prototypes.text: Repeated forceful physical contact directed at another person or animal, including pushing, striking, kicking, restraining, or pursuing as the target tries to withdraw.
One or more people control, pull, carry, or strike a vulnerable person or animal using hands, leashes, ropes, sticks, walls, beds, or mobility equipment.
An initially tense interaction escalates through repeated contact and resistance, followed by pursuit, falling, continued restraint, attempted escape, or intervention by nearby people.
Visible physical confrontations occur around homes, enclosed yards, roads, care environments, or public spaces, with bystanders, vehicles, barriers, or household equipment nearby.
Routine caregiving, leash handling, animal retrieval, or guiding someone away from danger remains coordinated and brief, unlike persistent force, pursuit, resistance, or visible distress.

candidate_prototypes.text: An adult repeatedly pushes, strikes, kicks, or restrains another person, causing them to stumble, fall, or remain on the ground while the interaction continues.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Across many scenes, forceful physical contact occurs in repeated sequences, followed by loss of balance, falls, restraint, or continued action on the ground.

candidate_prototypes.text: Caregivers or authority figures physically control children, older adults, or people with limited mobility near beds, cribs, wheelchairs, or walls, often during repeated handling.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Several scenes involve vulnerable people being held, repositioned, covered, pushed, or struck during caregiving, supervision, or institutional interactions.

candidate_prototypes.text: A confrontation escalates through repeated forceful contact, with the targeted person resisting, attempting to leave, or recovering, while bystanders or additional adults gather and sometimes intervene.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Recurring sequences show resistance or escape attempts, followed by renewed contact, group attention, restraint, intervention, or observers remaining nearby.

candidate_prototypes.text: People approach dogs or puppies, restrain them with leashes, ropes, or hands, then carry, pull, or load them away from homes and enclosed yards.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Several scenes show coordinated handling by one or more people, with animals moved across gates, over walls, or into a vehicle.

candidate_prototypes.text: A person pursues or strikes a dog, sometimes using a stick, after it retreats, hides, barks, or attempts to escape.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated interactions depict people applying force while dogs withdraw, resist, vocalize, or seek refuge near a house or enclosed area.

candidate_prototypes.text: Dogs, puppies, or children enter busy roadways, encounter moving vehicles, and are subsequently retrieved, carried, or guided away by nearby people as traffic pauses.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Multiple scenes combine vulnerable subjects, vehicle movement, immediate danger, and intervention by bystanders who remove or assist them.

final_prototypes.text: Uniformed officers approach a person during a tense encounter, physically restrain them, secure their hands with cuffs, and escort or hold them while monitoring the surroundings.
Officers make direct physical contact with a person, controlling their arms or body, applying restraint equipment, and coordinating with nearby personnel during containment.
The scene progresses from approach or pursuit, through resistance and physical control, to hand restraint, escort, detention, or continued supervision.
Visual context includes uniformed personnel, police vehicles, public roads or commercial areas, nearby bystanders, and a temporarily controlled space around people or vehicles.
Distinguish this from routine traffic stops or ordinary conversations by the combination of sustained physical control, secured hands, coordinated officers, and subsequent escort.

candidate_prototypes.text: Police officers approach a person after a tense interaction, physically restrain them, apply handcuffs, and escort or hold them while another officer monitors the scene.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated scenes show coordinated officer intervention, physical control, handcuffing, and continued supervision of a person.

candidate_prototypes.text: At a shop counter, a person confronts clerks with a handheld object, returns or lingers nearby, and is eventually subdued by officers using restraint equipment.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Several indoor sequences involve counter interactions, threatening gestures with an object, repeated presence, and later intervention by officers.

candidate_prototypes.text: A vehicle encounters police cars on a roadway, reverses or changes direction, and departs; elsewhere, a pursuing car follows a fast vehicle onto a side road.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Roadway sequences repeatedly show police vehicles following, stopping, reversing, turning, and continuing after another vehicle.

candidate_prototypes.text: Uniformed officers approach a person, physically push or hold them down, secure their hands, and later move or escort them while bystanders gather.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated sequences show officers transitioning from confrontation to physical restraint, hand control, removal, and crowd observation.

candidate_prototypes.text: Police vehicles follow or surround a moving car, forcing it to stop, while officers approach occupants and traffic or bystanders remain nearby.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Vehicle pursuits commonly end with blocking, abrupt stopping, officer convergence, and surrounding road users.

candidate_prototypes.text: An armed or threatening person faces officers with firearms, then falls or is subdued; officers inspect the scene and sometimes use a stretcher or escort them away.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Several scenes depict armed standoffs followed by a person falling, being controlled, and receiving movement or medical assistance.

final_prototypes.text: A person or group deliberately applies combustible liquid or burning material to structures, vehicles, or furnishings, ignites it, and departs as flames develop.
Individuals handle containers, fuel, paper, or ignition sources near surfaces, spreading combustible material before producing visible flames and smoke across adjacent objects.
Activity progresses from approach and material placement to ignition, expanding flames and smoke, withdrawal or escape, and later observation, suppression, or residual burning.
Scenes show enclosed rooms, entrances, vehicles, or outdoor areas where combustible items are positioned together and fire visibly affects nearby surfaces, furnishings, or structures.
Distinguish deliberate placement and ignition followed by spreading flames from forced entry alone, routine cooking or heating, and brief lighter use without sustained spread.

candidate_prototypes.text: A person applies a flammable liquid from a bucket or container to vehicles, doors, windows, walls, or furnishings, then ignites the treated area and withdraws.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Liquid application followed by ignition recurs across vehicles, buildings, rooms, and household objects.

candidate_prototypes.text: Individuals ignite paper, lighter flames, or other burning materials in enclosed or roadside spaces; flames and smoke persist, spread across nearby surfaces, and may later diminish or reappear.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Small ignition sources repeatedly develop into sustained burning and visible smoke across varied environments.

candidate_prototypes.text: After ignition, people commonly run or drive away, while flames continue around vehicles, buildings, rooms, or outdoor areas; bystanders or firefighters sometimes arrive to observe, spray water, or inspect.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Withdrawal after ignition is frequent, followed in some scenes by continued burning and later response activity.

candidate_prototypes.text: A group approaches secured doors, uses hand tools to defeat the locks, opens successive barriers, and enters the building.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Coordinated actions center on overcoming multiple entry barriers before the group moves inside.

candidate_prototypes.text: After entering, people distribute a flammable liquid near an entrance and across interior furnishings, then visible flames spread inward through the structure.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: The sequence links deliberate liquid placement with subsequent flame growth from an exterior threshold into the interior.

candidate_prototypes.text: A coordinated group forces entry with striking, prying, and kicking motions, enters briefly, leaves, and is followed by fire spreading through the building.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: This captures the temporal progression from collective access attempts to interior presence, departure, and later fire spread.

final_prototypes.text: Multiple people visibly converge on and physically strike, kick, push, or restrain one individual, often causing the person to fall while others gather nearby.
Participants use hands or carried objects to grab, pull, block, or hit a targeted person, while surrounding individuals join, watch closely, or attempt to separate them.
A sudden approach develops into repeated physical contact; the targeted person falls or becomes unable to move, followed by intervention, assistance, separation, or dispersal.
The pattern occurs in shared indoor or outdoor spaces where several people cluster around one person, restrict movement, and maintain close physical contact.
Distinguish from brief accidental contact, consensual play, or organized sports by the repeated directed actions, imbalance of participants, and visible loss of mobility.

candidate_prototypes.text: Several people surround and repeatedly punch, kick, or strike one person with sticks or other objects, knocking him down; interveners separate participants, but renewed contact often follows.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated group attacks, object use, falls, and attempted intervention recur across many settings.

candidate_prototypes.text: A group confronts an individual in doorways, offices, yards, or rooms, blocking movement, pulling or holding him, and sometimes forcing him inside or outside while others gather.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Multiple sequences show collective blocking, restraint, forced movement, and surrounding bystanders.

candidate_prototypes.text: After repeated strikes, the targeted person commonly remains on the ground or appears incapacitated, while bystanders approach, check, lift, separate participants, or disperse as the sequence ends.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Episodes frequently conclude with an injured person down and others providing attention or ending the confrontation.

candidate_prototypes.text: A person suddenly approaches or rushes toward another, pushes or strikes them, often knocking them down, then quickly retreats while nearby people remain present or move away.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated scenes show a brief, sudden physical interaction followed by rapid departure and continued movement among nearby people.

candidate_prototypes.text: Several people converge on one individual near a road or vehicle, surround and repeatedly strike or restrain the person, with the group dispersing after the person is grounded.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Multiple descriptions feature group participation, close surrounding, continued physical contact, and departure after the targeted person is down.

candidate_prototypes.text: After the confrontation, the affected person remains on the ground or appears injured while companions, bystanders, or responders approach, inspect them, or help them leave.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Later moments repeatedly show others checking the affected person, offering assistance, or gathering around after the physical interaction ends.

final_prototypes.text: People approach secured buildings, test or force doors and windows, enter through openings, and move through interior spaces while examining multiple areas.
Individuals manipulate locks, tools, bags, cabinets, drawers, and portable objects, with partners watching, illuminating, receiving items, or guiding them toward an exit.
The sequence progresses from scouting or testing access, to forced entry, systematic interior searching, selection and transport of objects, and departure or return.
Visual settings include homes, offices, shops, or storage areas where access points show tampering and interior spaces are searched beyond ordinary movement.
Distinguish from routine visitors, employees, deliveries, or maintenance by covert timing, coordinated access manipulation, persistent searching, and removal of multiple unrelated objects.

candidate_prototypes.text: People approach residential or office entrances, inspect or test doors and windows, then force openings or climb through and move inside to search multiple rooms.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated sequences show deliberate entrance attempts followed by interior movement and examination.

candidate_prototypes.text: After entry, people search cabinets, desks, rooms, appliances, and display areas, gather electronics, containers, furniture, or other objects, and carry or pass them toward an exit.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Interior searching frequently progresses into collecting, moving, and organizing assorted objects for removal.

candidate_prototypes.text: Groups often work in pairs or more, with one person watching, holding a light, handling tools, or receiving objects while another searches, pries, or transports items.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Multiple-person sequences repeatedly divide observation, entry work, searching, and object handling among participants.

candidate_prototypes.text: Multiple people force open a glass shop entrance with tools or vehicles, enter together, and move directly toward cash machines, safes, cabinets, or merchandise.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated across shops: coordinated entry follows door damage, with attention focused on valuable fixtures and stored goods.

candidate_prototypes.text: A vehicle repeatedly rams or backs through an entrance, while several people attach ropes and pull heavy fixtures or machines toward the vehicle for removal.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Several sequences show vehicle-assisted access followed by coordinated efforts to extract large, fixed objects.

candidate_prototypes.text: After entering, individuals search counters, drawers, cabinets, shelves, or enclosed rooms, place selected objects into bags or vehicles, and sometimes leave and return during the sequence.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Recurring interior activity combines systematic searching with carrying goods away in containers or transport vehicles.

final_prototypes.text: A sudden intense flash or ignition rapidly produces an expanding burst of flames, smoke, dust, or fragments, followed by lingering airborne material and disrupted surroundings.
People, vehicles, or nearby objects are abruptly affected by the blast, scattering, stopping, or being enveloped as observers and responders approach afterward.
Brief concentrated illumination or ignition is followed by rapid outward expansion, rising debris or smoke, sustained suspension, and gradual settling or suppression.
Outdoor spaces, roadsides, vehicles, structures, or open ground show a localized high-energy event with obscured visibility, scattered material, and lingering smoke.
Distinguish ordinary vehicle exhaust, dust from movement, controlled flames, or bright reflections by the abrupt flash, forceful expansion, debris dispersal, and persistent plume.

candidate_prototypes.text: A sudden bright flash is followed by dust, soil, and rocks rising and remaining suspended, with the frame dominated by airborne particulate debris and no visible people or vehicles.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Summarizes the repeated temporal sequence of bright illumination followed by lingering airborne ground material.

candidate_prototypes.text: A concentrated luminous event precedes a forceful spray of earth and stones, creating a sustained cloud of suspended material that continues across the recorded interval.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Emphasizes the transition from a brief bright occurrence to persistent dispersed debris.

candidate_prototypes.text: Bright illumination rapidly transitions into widespread airborne ground debris, including dust, soil, and rocks, while the environment remains visually focused on lingering particles.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Highlights the dominant visual presence and continued suspension of particulate material.

candidate_prototypes.text: A vehicle or fuel-related object suddenly ignites near active traffic, producing intense flames and smoke while nearby vehicles stop and occupants or bystanders move away.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Several scenes show abrupt ignition involving vehicles, followed by visible flames, smoke, stopped traffic, and people creating distance.

candidate_prototypes.text: Responders arrive after visible flames spread around a vehicle or doorway, deploy hoses or extinguishers, and progressively reduce the fire while smoke lingers.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Multiple descriptions include organized responses using water equipment or extinguishers, with suppression occurring gradually as smoke remains visible.

candidate_prototypes.text: Following a sudden burst or ignition, people gather, inspect the affected vehicle, reposition nearby equipment, and resume coordinated water handling as surrounding traffic continues.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Recurring later actions include approaching or inspecting affected vehicles, managing response equipment, and continuing activity amid passing traffic.

final_prototypes.text: Multiple people engage in rapid, forceful physical contact, including pushing, striking, grappling, and kicking, with one or more participants sometimes falling amid a crowded confrontation.
Participants grab, wield, or raise nearby chairs, stools, bottles, sticks, or other objects during heated confrontations, while surrounding people intervene, restrain participants, or move away.

A verbal disagreement escalates into repeated physical contact as additional people arrive, participants surround or restrain someone, and the episode ends with separation, dispersal, or renewed convergence.
Such incidents occur near entrances, storefronts, streets, rooms, vehicle areas, or social spaces, with bystanders gathering, watching, checking fallen individuals, or attempting to restore distance.

Separate forceful, sustained clashes involving grabbing, striking, kicking, or wrestling from ordinary conversation, brief accidental contact, playful activity, or coordinated sports movement without visible disruption.

candidate_prototypes.text: Two or more adults rapidly approach, grab, push, strike, or wrestle with one another inside a store or near a doorway, while bystanders gather and intervene.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated close physical confrontations occur in commercial interiors and entrances, with additional people observing, restraining participants, or pulling them apart.

candidate_prototypes.text: Participants raise or use chairs, stools, sticks, bottles, knives, hammers, axes, or other nearby objects during a heated confrontation, followed by restraint or removal.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Several scenes show escalating interactions involving handheld objects, then intervention by bystanders, guards, or officers who control and escort a participant.

candidate_prototypes.text: A disagreement develops after people exit or approach vehicles, continues beside a car or at an entrance, and ends with participants separating, running away, or dispersing.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Outdoor and threshold encounters repeatedly transition from verbal gestures to physical contact before vehicles depart or people leave in different directions.

candidate_prototypes.text: Multiple people converge around a dispute, with repeated pushing, punches, kicks, and grappling; one or more participants fall, while others watch, intervene, or move away.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Recurring scenes show direct physical contact escalating from a smaller dispute into group involvement, followed by falls, observation, intervention, or dispersal.

candidate_prototypes.text: A one-on-one confrontation escalates as additional participants arrive, surround or restrain someone, and continue physical contact before the group disperses and later regathers.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Many sequences follow a repeated temporal pattern: an initial exchange, expanding participation, attempts to control individuals, and later regrouping or departure.

candidate_prototypes.text: Physical clashes recur in streets, rooms, counters, or social spaces, sometimes involving furniture or handheld objects, followed by separation, checking a fallen participant, or departure.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: The recurring action is visible across varied settings and may include nearby objects, while the closing moments often show separation, assistance, inspection, or people leaving.

final_prototypes.text: People routinely walk, work, browse, sort, carry, exchange, and arrange everyday items, with vehicles and pedestrians moving through shared spaces in orderly, recurring activity.

Individuals handle merchandise, documents, packages, tools, carts, and personal belongings while cooperating with clerks, coworkers, customers, drivers, or companions at counters, tables, shelves, and vehicles.

Activity unfolds through repeated arrivals, departures, brief pauses, exchanges, loading, browsing, travel, and resumed movement, with participants completing tasks and leaving or continuing naturally.
Indoor workplaces, stores, corridors, homes, parking areas, roads, and fueling points support routine pedestrian flow, vehicle movement, shopping, work, waiting, and brief social interaction.

Ordinary activity shows steady movement, proportional gestures, cooperative handling, and uninterrupted task completion, without sudden confrontational behavior, forced taking, hazardous damage, or persistent disorder.

candidate_prototypes.text: Workers and visitors repeatedly enter and leave shops, offices, kitchens, and storage areas while packing, sorting, shelving, carrying, and arranging goods around tables, counters, boxes, and carts.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Many scenes show continuous movement through work areas combined with practical handling and organization of merchandise or supplies.

candidate_prototypes.text: Small groups perform routine manual tasks over time: moving containers, loading shelves, operating carts or machines, organizing work surfaces, and returning to continue coordinated handling.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: The descriptions frequently depict several people sharing workplaces and completing sequential material-handling tasks.

candidate_prototypes.text: People commonly exchange papers, packages, books, food, or small objects at counters and tables, with brief conversations, inspections, payments, and departures interspersed among ongoing work.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated interactions involve presenting, checking, transferring, or receiving items during ordinary commercial and workplace activity.

candidate_prototypes.text: Cars and vans enter parking areas, adjust position through forward or backward movements, turn, stop, and eventually leave while other vehicles pass nearby.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated vehicle maneuvers include parking, reversing, turning, pausing, and departing within shared lots, roads, garages, and gated entrances.

candidate_prototypes.text: People approach parked vehicles, enter or exit, walk across the surrounding area, retrieve or place items, and return while vehicles remain stationary or depart.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Multiple scenes show routine interaction between pedestrians and vehicles, including walking, loading, checking interiors, and leaving after brief stops.

candidate_prototypes.text: At roadside or fueling locations, vehicles arrive and stop while people refuel, pay, open doors, wait nearby, and resume travel as surrounding traffic continues.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Recurring roadside activity combines vehicle arrivals, service or fueling actions, short pedestrian movements, and ongoing passage of other cars and trucks.

candidate_prototypes.text: Pedestrians repeatedly enter, leave, cross, or walk along roadside and corridor areas in both directions, often singly or in pairs and small groups.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Across many sequences, people continuously traverse shared outdoor paths, sidewalks, intersections, and passageways with varied pacing and group sizes.

candidate_prototypes.text: Road traffic passes intermittently while pedestrians pause, cross, converse, use phones, carry belongings, walk dogs, or accompany children, strollers, and shopping carts.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: The recurring activity combines ordinary pedestrian movement with brief interactions, family accompaniment, carried items, and changing vehicle flow.

candidate_prototypes.text: People gather near doorways, shops, houses, vehicles, or roadside goods, entering and exiting, loading items, opening doors, talking, and then continuing onward.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Multiple scenes show short-duration stops around entrances, parked vehicles, carts, luggage, packages, or merchandise before participants disperse.

candidate_prototypes.text: Customers approach store counters, present products or papers, exchange money, cards, or change with clerks, receive packaged goods, and depart while others wait nearby.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Counter-based purchasing repeatedly involves payment, item exchange, packaging, and orderly customer departures.

candidate_prototypes.text: People enter and leave continuously, browse shelves or freezers, inspect and select merchandise, carry bags or goods, and move between aisles and checkout areas.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Recurring movement combines browsing, product selection, carrying purchases, and transitions through the store.

candidate_prototypes.text: Clerks remain behind counters, sorting, scanning, cleaning, labeling, restocking, packaging, and handing over merchandise while answering questions and coordinating with customers or coworkers.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Staff repeatedly organize merchandise and support transactions through preparation, assistance, communication, and handover.

candidate_prototypes.text: Multiple people continuously walk through halls, corridors, malls, terminals, or exhibition spaces, passing one another and maintaining a steady flow across the visible indoor area.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated descriptions emphasize sustained pedestrian movement through shared indoor public spaces, with individuals crossing at different times or simultaneously.

candidate_prototypes.text: Individuals enter through doors, cross rooms or hallways, and leave or disappear from view, with arrivals and departures occurring at separate moments throughout the sequence.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Several scenes repeatedly show people using doorways, traversing an interior, and exiting or moving beyond the visible area.

candidate_prototypes.text: Small groups pause to talk, gather, or coordinate while other people continue walking nearby; some interact with tables, counters, stairs, workstations, or everyday objects.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Recurring scenes combine pedestrian traffic with brief conversations, group gatherings, and practical interactions with furnishings or nearby objects.

candidate_prototypes.text: Multiple cars, vans, trucks, buses, motorcycles, bicycles, and electric vehicles travel through roads and intersections in different directions, with vehicles entering, passing, turning, stopping, and leaving over time.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated descriptions show steady mixed traffic moving through roads and junctions, with varied vehicle types following different routes and gradually leaving the scene.

candidate_prototypes.text: Pedestrians regularly walk or cross near moving traffic, while riders on bicycles, motorcycles, and electric vehicles approach, wait, turn, or continue along the roadside and through intersections.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: People and riders repeatedly share roadside spaces with vehicles, crossing, walking, waiting, or traveling through the same traffic areas.

candidate_prototypes.text: Roadside activity includes vehicles pausing, reversing, parking, loading, refueling, or exchanging items, with drivers and pedestrians interacting briefly before traffic resumes and vehicles depart.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Several scenes combine short vehicle stops with boarding, unloading, refueling, directing, handling goods, or brief exchanges before movement continues.

candidate_prototypes.text: Vehicles repeatedly travel through busy roads and intersections in both directions, forming steady flows, queues, and occasional turns while parked or waiting vehicles remain nearby.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Most scenes show sustained roadway movement with vehicles passing in groups, waiting at intersections, and turning onto adjoining lanes.

candidate_prototypes.text: Pedestrians routinely walk beside roads or cross between traffic, sometimes in groups or with bicycles, umbrellas, bags, or dogs, while vehicles continue passing.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: People frequently appear alongside moving traffic, crossing streets, walking near parked vehicles, or entering nearby buildings.

candidate_prototypes.text: Cars, buses, trucks, vans, motorcycles, and other transport vehicles arrive at intervals, stop, reverse, park, merge, or turn through connected lanes and parking areas.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Recurring vehicle actions include stopping, reversing, parking, lane changes, merging, and turning amid mixed transport types.

candidate_prototypes.text: People move through indoor rooms and doorways, pausing to talk, gesture, handle personal items, and sometimes sit briefly before leaving or returning.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Across many scenes, individuals repeatedly enter, exit, pause near doors, communicate with others, and resume movement through adjoining areas.

candidate_prototypes.text: Individuals work at counters, tables, shelves, or computer stations while sorting, examining, exchanging, carrying, or placing objects during routine interactions.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Workstation and storage-area scenes commonly involve handling folders, bags, boxes, envelopes, devices, or other items while speaking with nearby people.

candidate_prototypes.text: People wait or pace indoors, check phones, adjust belongings, operate switches, and use brief gestures while rooms periodically become quiet or empty.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Several sequences combine short periods of waiting, personal adjustments, phone use, lighting changes, and temporary absence after others depart.

candidate_prototypes.text: Customers repeatedly enter and leave stores singly or in groups, passing through doorways, greeting others, browsing nearby areas, and sometimes returning after briefly exiting.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Frequent pedestrian circulation and doorway transitions recur across stores and mall corridors.

candidate_prototypes.text: Shoppers select, inspect, carry, exchange, or return merchandise, then approach counters to communicate with clerks, pay, receive change, or organize purchased goods.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Browsing and routine counter interactions appear consistently throughout the shopping scenes.

candidate_prototypes.text: Staff and customers organize shelves, counters, carts, bags, and scattered items while others browse, converse, push carts, carry packages, or move between aisles.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Routine arranging, carrying, cleaning, and shared movement accompany ordinary retail activity.

candidate_prototypes.text: People occupy office workstations, completing computer-based tasks, reviewing papers, typing, speaking briefly, and remaining engaged for extended periods.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated scenes show employees seated at desks while working with computers, documents, and nearby colleagues.

candidate_prototypes.text: Staff and visitors routinely enter, leave, cross rooms, approach desks or counters, and pause to communicate with seated personnel.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Many descriptions include recurring movement through office areas, room entrances, counters, and workstations alongside short interactions.

candidate_prototypes.text: Individuals exchange documents, phones, and small items while others organize materials, move between seats, and continue ordinary office activity.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Handling papers and objects commonly occurs alongside conversations, sorting, filing, and continued work by surrounding employees.

final_prototypes.text: Moving vehicles unexpectedly collide with other vehicles, vulnerable road users, or roadside objects, causing abrupt stops, falls, overturning, displacement, or scattered debris.
Vehicles make forceful contact with cars, motorcycles, bicycles, pedestrians, barriers, trees, or structures, while occupants or nearby people are struck, displaced, trapped, or knocked down.
Normal traffic movement is interrupted by contact, followed by falling or displaced people, stopped vehicles, gathering bystanders, assistance, inspection, and possible departure.
Roadways, intersections, turns, crossings, and roadside areas contain moving or parked vehicles, nearby pedestrians, and continuing traffic around a sudden disruptive event.
Routine traffic, close passes, turning, parking, or brief stops retain controlled movement and upright road users without forceful contact, falls, displacement, or gathering.

candidate_prototypes.text: Vehicles traveling on roads suddenly collide with other cars, trucks, motorcycles, roadside structures, barriers, or trees, sometimes overturning, stopping, reversing, or leaving the scene.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated sequences show moving vehicles making forceful contact, followed by changed positions, damaged surroundings, and continued traffic nearby.

candidate_prototypes.text: Pedestrians or bystanders in or beside the roadway are hit by moving vehicles, knocked down, trapped, or thrown, while others run toward them.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Multiple descriptions depict people occupying travel paths and subsequent crowd movement toward injured or displaced individuals.

candidate_prototypes.text: After a collision, drivers and passersby exit or approach, inspect vehicles, make phone calls, assist occupants, move debris, and gather around the roadside scene.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Post-impact activity repeatedly involves checking vehicles, helping people, communicating, and remaining near the affected area.

candidate_prototypes.text: A moving car or other motor vehicle contacts a motorcycle at an intersection or turn, throwing riders down or toward the roadside while traffic slows and vehicles remain nearby.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated interactions involve turning or crossing vehicles contacting motorcycles, followed by rider falls and disrupted roadway movement.

candidate_prototypes.text: After a roadway collision, riders or pedestrians lie on the ground, then nearby drivers, passengers, and passersby approach, inspect them, and sometimes help lift or move them.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Many sequences continue with people gathering, checking fallen individuals, and providing physical assistance beside stopped vehicles.

candidate_prototypes.text: A vehicle strikes one or more road users, followed by people gathering around the involved vehicles, riders recovering or being assisted, and occasional departure of a driver or vehicle.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: The recurring temporal pattern combines vehicle contact, immediate crowd response, recovery by affected people, and changing vehicle presence.

candidate_prototypes.text: A vehicle turns, reverses, or moves forward into another parked or moving vehicle, with both remaining visible before the striking vehicle changes position or leaves.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated across scenes involving cars, trucks, and buses, with contact followed by backing away, departure, or continued repositioning.

candidate_prototypes.text: A moving car or bus enters a roadside area, contacts one or more pedestrians, and then continues away while people scatter, walk, or briefly pursue it.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Several sequences pair vehicle movement with pedestrian contact, followed by dispersal, observation, or pursuit near the roadway.

candidate_prototypes.text: A vehicle skids, reverses, or turns into a railing, wall, building, tree, barrier, or roundabout, sometimes contacting multiple objects in succession.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated scenes show a vehicle leaving its intended path or maneuvering space before striking roadside structures or several nearby vehicles.

candidate_prototypes.text: Vehicles traveling through intersections or roadways suddenly collide while other traffic continues moving, sometimes involving turning, crossing, or approaching vehicles and producing overturned or displaced vehicles.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Repeated descriptions center on two or more moving vehicles making contact amid active traffic, especially at intersections.

candidate_prototypes.text: A moving car strikes a motorcycle, bicycle, tricycle, or pedestrian during a turn or crossing, followed by the affected road user falling, being displaced, or remaining in roadway.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Recurring interactions involve vehicles contacting vulnerable road users during roadway crossings, turns, or movement through intersections.

candidate_prototypes.text: After a collision, bystanders or vehicle occupants run toward the scene, gather around affected vehicles, assist people or overturned objects, while traffic slows, stops, or continues nearby.
candidate_prototypes.rationale: Several sequences show an immediate human response around impacted vehicles, alongside changing traffic movement and temporary roadway obstruction.

final_prototypes.text: One or more armed or forceful individuals confront people, demand valuables or access, collect money or goods, and depart rapidly from the location.
Individuals threaten or restrain occupants while opening registers, drawers, cabinets, bags, or containers and transferring cash, merchandise, phones, or personal belongings.
The sequence develops from coordinated approach and intimidation to compelled compliance, searching or collection of valuables, followed by hurried withdrawal and possible pursuit.
Visual settings include staffed counters, stores, residences, roadside encounters, or stopped vehicles where multiple people control occupants and access personal or commercial property.
Distinguish routine purchasing, browsing, or ordinary workplace interactions from coercive demands, forced access, restrained occupants, hurried collection of property, and coordinated departure.

candidate_prototypes.text: An armed person approaches a staffed counter, points a gun, directs the attendant to provide cash or items, then quickly departs.
